Seller’s discretionary earnings (SDE) can add back one owner’s compensation and benefits, interest, depreciation, amortization and selected discretionary or nonrecurring expenses. These ratios are not net profit after replacing a working owner with a manager.

Convenience stores exclude gas station listings. Cleaning businesses and laundromats have different service mixes and owner workloads.

A higher SDE ratio does not establish higher annual dollar profit, lower investment, or greater return on capital. Replacement management, ongoing capital expenditure and debt service must be assessed separately.

metricDefinitions.label: Opening expenses
metricDefinitions.definition: Analyst allowance for deposits, fit-out, equipment/vehicles, opening inventory, permits, professional fees and pre-opening marketing. metricDefinitions.label: Cash reserve
metricDefinitions.definition: Six months × analyst monthly fixed-cost/payroll/working-capital liquidity allowance. This is ring-fenced capital, not a second operating expense charge or a full year of expenses. Actual peak cash deficit requires a monthly ramp/cash-flow model.

metricDefinitions.label: Total startup funds
metricDefinitions.definition: Opening allowance + six-month reserve; range is a planning scenario, not a confidence interval or a measured typical cost. Bar uses arithmetic midpoint solely for sorting/display.

caveats: All 66 startup ranges are judgment-based planning assumptions, not vendor quotes, survey medians, valuations or company-specific costs. General SBA guidance and franchisor examples inform cost categories only; they do not validate these category estimates.
Startup format/size does not match the national established-business sale sample. Earnings are not a first-year forecast. Do not divide these two datasets to infer ROI or payback.

Leased premises/land where applicable; no real estate purchase, acquisition goodwill, franchise fees, financing, owner personal cash needs, major environmental remediation or unusual site works. Very site-specific property businesses need detailed local estimates.
Range combines low opening with low liquidity and high opening with high liquidity. Arithmetic midpoint is a display convention, not a likely price.

evidenceFlow.title: Cost structure, not category price evidence
evidenceFlow.detail: SBA startup-cost guidance separates opening and ongoing needs. Official Scooter’s Coffee, Anytime Fitness and Meineke pages demonstrate format-dependent investment; none is asserted to quote the 66 independent formats.

evidenceFlow.title: Explicit planning inputs
evidenceFlow.detail: update-startup-planning.py contains 66 analyst-authored opening and monthly liquidity ranges in thousands of US dollars, each with a named format. Fixed six-month reserve; no inflation/location adjustment claimed.

evidenceFlow.title: Funds and range midpoint
evidenceFlow.detail: startup_low = opening_low + 6 × monthly_liquidity_low; startup_high = opening_high + 6 × monthly_liquidity_high; startup_mid = (startup_low + startup_high) / 2.

metricDefinitions.label: 5-year survival benchmark
metricDefinitions.definition: Share of the mapped broad US private-industry establishment opening cohort still open after five years. Remaining open is not profitability or personal success probability.

metricDefinitions.label: Demand / availability proxy
metricDefinitions.definition: Expected locations at US per-resident employer-location density divided by reported local locations. It assumes equal demand per resident and output per location; actual customer demand/capacity is not measured.

metricDefinitions.definition: BLS 2025 annual-average private UI-covered employer establishments at mapped NAICS; not current competitors, licensed beds, staffed slots, companies or self-employed providers.

source.label: Local employer-location density and national industry survival benchmarks
caveats: Year2025 annual averages, not current2026 operating census.
Employer-only; self-employed/nonemployer competition excluded.
A site count is not service slots, beds, revenue, floor area, machines, staffing, throughput or waiting demand.
BLS establishment reporting units differ from brands/legalbusinesses/physical service locations.
NezPerce+Asotin captures Lewiston-Clarkston vicinity but includes rural/outlying places and omits regional/inbound/online competition.
Same broad category may map to multiple dashboard rows; do not sum these rows.
Mapped NAICS can be broader or narrower than the portfolio business-sale category; each row discloses its scope.
Index is particularly weak for export manufacturing, tourism, professional national work, B2B or healthcare appointment/bed capacity.
Expected counts are analyst calculations from national density, not survey forecasts or local spending estimates.
Survival is measured at the establishment/site level, not enterprise/owner level; a chain opening a branch is an establishment opening.
No causal local success probability, profitability, return on investment or owner income can be inferred.
The employment-based administrative population does not represent all sole-proprietor/nonemployer businesses.
The same broad-sector benchmark intentionally repeats across business formats in that sector.
Business-format classifications are explicit assumptions; changes in format may change the mapped sector.
Native raw file download blocked with HTTP 403; web primary-source extraction receipts and relevant cohort extracts retained.
The actual customer-demand to staffed-capacity ratio is unmeasured for every business. Density is an assumption-based screen, not a shortage measurement.
100% means national employer-location density parity; 200% means half that density locally, not two customers for every available service.
The county and two-county metro are not Lewiston city boundaries; regional demand crosses both. US per-capita demand and output per location may differ from local conditions.
Several labels map to the same or overlapping NAICS categories; never sum row counts across all business types.
Missing county/industry components are unknown; ratios remain null rather than assuming zero. Published employer establishment counts may remain available when jobs/wages are suppressed.
Survival does not imply profitability. Broad industry survival is not an independent business-type rate or a local/personal success probability.
Only UI-covered private employers are counted. Self-employed/nonemployer competitors, outlet scale, service capacity, staffing, price and qualified waitlists are not captured.
